result.description: Graph database platform; Aura cloud API manages instances and Query API runs Cypher over HTTP.
result.auth_detail: Aura management REST API itself (api.neo4j.io): OAuth 2.0 client-credentials. Client ID/secret from Aura Console go as HTTP Basic to POST /oauth/token. Returns 1-hour bearer token for the Authorization header. Database access (Query API/Bolt): username/password Basic, or bearer token from SSO/OIDC on Enterprise/Aura. MCP server login is separate and not the basis for this.
result.access_detail: Aura API credentials creatable on all tiers. AuraDB Free is $0 with no credit card. Free/trial accounts rate-limited to 25 req/min; 125 req/min on paid tiers.
result.api_notes: Aura API v1 (api.neo4j.io) manages instances, plus billing endpoints in v2beta1; full endpoint list is in the OpenAPI spec. I did not fetch the spec, so I can't confirm the exact endpoint count. Query API runs Cypher over HTTPS and is enabled by default. I did not read the Query API auth page, so its auth methods come from the MCP docs and general knowledge.

evidence.quote: The Aura API uses OAuth 2.0 for API authentication.
Authentication to the token endpoint uses HTTP Basic Authentication, where the client ID and client secret are provided as the username and password, respectively.
All tiers can create Aura API credentials.
No credit card or other payment method required
The Aura API allows you to programmatically perform actions on your Aura instances without the need to log in to the Console.
The Query API allows to execute Cypher statements against a Neo4j server through HTTP requests.
The bearer token is obtained from your identity provider and passed to Neo4j for authentication.
Authentication runs through the Aura Console using a human-in-the-loop OAuth redirect.
